To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most common causes of pain were musculoskeletal injuries (43%), headache (17%), chest pain (10%), abdominal pain (10%) and back pain (8%).

the most common causes of pain in the emergency department were abdominal and musculoskeletal, the most common pain medication was intravenous opioids, and patient satisfaction was associated with pain intensity, time to pain relief, pain management practices, and patient expectations.
pain is the primary presenting complaint in 30% of patients presenting to the Emergency Department (ED), and that pain is inadequately managed in 50% of these patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the etiology of the disease.
the development of a model that will allow the prediction and management of pain in patients presenting to emergency departments with a wide variety of conditions.
the development of a model that will help to predict the outcome of a patient's pain experience.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the emergency physician should be able to manage the vast majority of patients who present to the emergency department with pain.
pain is a multidimensional phenomenon and that pain assessment is a complex process.
the use of opioids in the management of pain has increased significantly since 1999 and that there is no evidence that this has resulted in an increase in opioid abuse or addiction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and validated a new tool, the Pain Management Assessment Tool (PMAT), that is useful in assessing and improving pain management in the ED.
the emergency department (ED) is the most frequent place for patients with acute pain to seek treatment, but the pain is frequently undertreated.
the results of this study suggest that the emergency departments in the study were not adequately addressing the pain needs of patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is an opportunity to improve pain management in emergency department settings.
the use of a standardized protocol for the management of patients with pain in an ED setting is associated with an improvement in the quality of the pain management.

there is a need to develop and implement a standardized protocol for pain management in the ED that includes a pain score assessment, pain medication administration and documentation of the patient's pain score before and after treatment.
